name: Arm Extraction and Pass
description: Against Crackhead Control, open the high-leg clinch and recover the elbow before passing. Clearing the arm alone does not establish a completed guard pass.
summary: Arm extraction against Crackhead Control opens the high-leg enclosure, recovers an inside elbow and only then begins a separate guard pass.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The arm must come free before passing. The two-leg clinch does not guarantee either a shoulder lock or an immediate side-control opening.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).

attacker.name: Arm Extraction and Pass Attacker
attacker.description: Arm Extraction and Pass (attacker): Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.
attacker.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The arm must come free before passing. The two-leg clinch does not guarantee either a shoulder lock or an immediate side-control opening.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Create slack at the hip and thigh while keeping the head and captured arm aligned. Withdraw the shoulder and elbow only after the high leg connection has opened. Establish side control after a completed guard pass only when the upper-body enclosure and relevant leg hooks have cleared.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The arm escape comes before hip control for the pass: recover the elbow from the high-leg clinch and any retained overhook first. After clearing both knees, a side pin can use crossface shoulder pressure and balanced chest pressure while the hip block prevents the knees returning.

Protect the captured limb: A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.

Open the high enclosure: Create slack at the hip and thigh while keeping the head and captured arm aligned.
Recover the elbow and posture: Withdraw the shoulder and elbow only after the high leg connection has opened.
Confirm the next position: Establish side control after a completed guard pass only when the upper-body enclosure and relevant leg hooks have cleared.

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): Which arm shape avoids offering a long lever to the high legs?
flashcards.answer: Keep the elbow compact while opening the high clinch; extending it between the legs can invite isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep the elbow bent near your ribs

plausible: Reach a straight arm between the high knees
Post the hand far behind the opponent's head
trap: Grip the ankle and straighten the trapped elbow

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): Your wrist moves but the extra leg holds you low; what must clear?
flashcards.answer: The second high leg reinforces the facing upper-body clinch and makes posture recovery harder. A mobile wrist does not prove that the shoulder has escaped this restraint; clear the high connection before withdrawing the arm.
flashcards.answer_line: The high-leg restraint around your shoulder line

plausible: Only the grip on the wrist that already moves
Only the lower foot resting at your waist
trap: Only your hand contact with the opponent's hip

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): Before high closure, how should the hip-side framing arm sit?
flashcards.answer: Use an early inside forearm at the hip or thigh while maintaining a balanced base. Keep the arm compact rather than reaching across the outside of the thigh. This is a preventive frame, not permission to move through a completed lock.
flashcards.answer_line: A bent forearm inside the hip or thigh line

plausible: A straight elbow extending past the outside of the thigh
A flared elbow with only the wrist touching the thigh
trap: An elbow pinned outside the knee while the hand reaches inward

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): How should your head and captured arm move as slack appears?
flashcards.answer: Create slack at the hip and thigh with the head and captured arm aligned, then use the opening rather than wrenching a trapped limb.
flashcards.answer_line: Stay aligned while opening space at hip and thigh

plausible: Turn the head away while the elbow stays fixed
Pull the wrist out while the shoulder stays pinned
trap: Raise the chest before the shoulder can follow

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): What must open before your elbow is withdrawn?
flashcards.answer: Withdraw the shoulder and elbow after the high leg connection opens around them, not by pulling a wrist through a fixed shoulder trap.
flashcards.answer_line: The high-leg connection around the shoulder

plausible: The wrist grip while the upper arm stays enclosed
The second high leg while the first still clamps
trap: A gap below the knee with the shoulder still caught

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): What establishes side control after your arm comes free?
flashcards.answer: Side control requires a completed leg clearance and stable chest contact beside the torso after the arm and high clinch are free.
flashcards.answer_line: Clear both knees; settle beside the chest

plausible: Raise the head while remaining between both knees
Clear one knee but leave the other leg hooking
trap: Clear both knees but leave the chest out of contact

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): In the starting Crackhead clinch, where is the opponent?
flashcards.answer: The performer is the top player facing a bottom guard player whose two high legs restrict the upper body.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing you from below, legs behind your head

plausible: Facing you below with the legs at waist level
Facing you below with one high shin and a low foot
trap: Facing you below with one shoulder in a leg triangle

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): What must clear before you turn to begin the guard pass?
flashcards.answer: Recover the elbow from the high-leg connection and any overhook before organizing hip control for the separate pass.
flashcards.answer_line: Free the elbow from the high clinch and overhook

plausible: Pin the hips while leaving the elbow enclosed
Crossface while your shoulder remains clamped
trap: Remove the wrist grip but leave the overhook intact

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): Your shoulder is fixed as you start circling; what now?
flashcards.answer: Do not circle around a fixed shoulder. Pause the passing movement and address the remaining high-leg or arm connection.

plausible: Keep the elbow still and rotate the torso
Pull the hand farther behind your hip
trap: Shift your knees around before opening the clamp

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): What shows successful arm clearance in a cooperative drill?
flashcards.answer: Check that the shoulder and elbow can move together outside the upper-body trap without loading the joint before rehearsing a pass.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder and elbow both clear the high trap

plausible: The hand moves while the upper arm stays pinned
The head lifts while the elbow remains caught
trap: One high leg drops while the other retains the arm

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): After knee clearance, which contact blocks their return at the hip?
flashcards.answer: Once the legs are cleared, a hip block and balanced chest contact help prevent the knees returning between the bodies.
flashcards.answer_line: A hip block beside stable chest contact

plausible: Chest contact with the hip-side elbow lifted
A hip block with the chest pulled away
trap: A crossface with both arms above the shoulder line

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (top): How does an elbow-knee barrier show the pass is incomplete?
flashcards.answer: Even with the arm free, an inside knee connected to the defender's elbow preserves a guard barrier that must be cleared before side control.
flashcards.answer_line: The defender still has a knee between your torsos

plausible: The defender's knees stay outside your hip line
The defender's forearm frames with both knees cleared
trap: The defender's elbow touches a knee behind your hips

defender.name: Arm Extraction and Pass Defender
defender.description: Arm Extraction and Pass (defender): Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Crackhead Control; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The arm must come free before passing. The two-leg clinch does not guarantee either a shoulder lock or an immediate side-control opening.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees. Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again. Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

If the high clinch opens, use a short hip escape while a forearm holds the shoulder away. Reconnect elbow and knee before the passer fills that gap; chasing the freed arm would abandon the guard recovery space.
key_principles: Start with broken posture: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg.
Bring the second leg high: Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
Track both elbows: Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.
Keep knees close: Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees.
Return to one-leg control: Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again.
Open against a stack: Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (bottom): What supports the clinch before adding your second leg?
flashcards.answer: Build the first high-leg and hand connection before adding the second leg behind the opponent's head.
flashcards.answer_line: The first high shin joined to its supporting hand

plausible: The first high shin with its hand already released
The second high leg before the first shin is secured
trap: A low ankle crossing beneath the shoulder line

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (bottom): How can the second high leg reinforce the clinch?
flashcards.answer: The reinforcing leg should follow a comfortable hip angle; do not force the foot against a fixed knee to retain the top player.
flashcards.answer_line: Lift it within a hip angle that supports the knee

plausible: Hold the knee still and haul the foot inward
Let the knee fall away as the foot climbs
trap: Lift the foot higher while keeping the hips flat

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (bottom): What must you check before treating the clinch as Dead Orchard?
flashcards.answer: Track both opposing elbows and the actual leg closure. Crackhead's reinforced clinch does not automatically become Dead Orchard.
flashcards.answer_line: Both arms are enclosed by a high leg figure-four

plausible: Only that both feet are above the shoulders
Only that one hand has reached the mat
trap: Only that the opponent cannot raise the chin

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (bottom): How do you retain space when the passer frees the arm?
flashcards.answer: As the clinch opens, frame the shoulder, make a short hip escape and reconnect elbow and knee before the passer fills the gap.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame the shoulder and reconnect elbow to knee

plausible: Chase the freed wrist with both arms extended
Keep both knees outside the passing torso
trap: Frame the shoulder but leave the hip-side knee behind

flashcards.question: Arm Extraction and Pass (bottom): How do you return to Mission Control during the extraction?
flashcards.answer: Return to one-leg control by lowering the reinforcing leg while keeping the original high shin and hand connected.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower the second leg while retaining the first shin grip

plausible: Drop both high legs before finding hand support
Keep the second leg high and release the first shin
trap: Lower the second leg while opening the first knee hug
